set.body:
Counted across the package: 986 stop() calls, zero cli/rlang conditions. Of those, 143 are
internal-invariant assertions phrased as '... are missing or noncanonical' (69) or '... is
inconsistent' (74). Roughly SIX tell the user what to type.

THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM is not tone. It is that internal assertions and user errors are
indistinguishable. A stopifnot-style invariant that should read as 'this is a bug in the package,
please report it' currently reads as 'you did something wrong', so users burn time trying to fix
conditions they cannot cause and cannot repair.

THE FIVE WORST, verbatim, with why:

1. R/scope.R:249-251, reached by swapping two arguments:
     plan_geometry(rel, over, at)
     Error: Frame fields are missing or noncanonical.
   The user passed a perfectly valid effect_pairing. Nothing was noncanonical - two arguments
   were backwards. Since at= and over= are opaque names that are not guessable in either
   direction, this is the most likely first error anyone makes, and the message actively
   misdirects toward frame corruption.

2. R/compiler.R:5-8:
     Opaque relation sources require explicit source_capabilities() before execution.
   Three framework nouns in eleven words. 'Opaque' is a property the user never declared - it
   means they passed a function instead of a matrix. Nothing says what to write.

3. R/geometry-plan.R:455-460:
     The conservative memory plan requires 3221225472 bytes, exceeding the 1073741824-byte budget.
   Raw bytes, no units, no remedy. All three real options - raise workspace_bytes, go query-first
   via evaluate_geometry, shrink the frame - go unmentioned. Same shape at R/crossnobis.R:161,
   R/residual-statistics.R:118, R/tomography.R:121.

4. R/evidence-api.R:13-21 - this one TRIES to advise and the advice is unusable:
     ... Use the support-local geometry plan; brain-scale measurement tomography is not yet exported.
   'The support-local geometry plan' is not the name of any exported function, and 'measurement
   tomography' appears in no user-facing document. The user is directed to something they cannot
   find, using a word that only exists inside the source tree - see also the 'tomography' entry in
   bd-01KZY8X53W0DQ8P99AD0V0CF7F, same leak.

5. R/task.R:50:
     Symmetric-packed atoms require a self-adjoint self-form task.
   Four framework terms, zero domain terms. codec, atom, self-adjoint and task are all internal;
   none is a concept the user chose or can change.

THE PACKAGE ALREADY KNOWS HOW TO DO THIS. Counter-examples from its own source:
  R/views.R:263        'The RSA design is rank deficient; remove redundant RDMs.'  - perfect
  R/execution.R:42     'workers > 1 is not implemented in effectagram 0.1; workers must be 1.'
  R/crossnobis.R:230   '... use noise_precision(diag(...)) for a fixed identity metric.'
                       - the ONLY message in 986 that contains runnable code
  R/neuroim2-adapter.R:10-13  names the required version AND the upstream commit
  R/crossnobis.R       'Crossnobis requires an explicit noise-precision metric schedule; an
                        implicit Euclidean geometry has no declared noise metric.' - requirement
                        plus reason

So the house style exists, is good, and is applied in five places out of 986.

PROPOSED, in order:
  1. Reclass the 143 invariant assertions as an internal-error condition that announces itself as
     a bug. Zero semantic risk, and it immediately stops users trying to repair them.
  2. Rewrite the ~40 REACHABLE messages on the R/crossnobis.R:230 template - requirement, reason,
     runnable fix. Example:
       before  Frame fields are missing or noncanonical.
       after   `at` must be a spatial frame (compile_frame(), voxels(), searchlights(), regions(),
               whole_brain()). You supplied an <effect_pairing> - that belongs in `over`.
  3. Add units and remedies to the four budget messages.

None of this touches semantics. It is the cheapest large accessibility win in the review after
tiering.
set.title: 986 stop() calls, 5 usable error messages, 143 internal invariants dressed as user errors
